responsibility:
`rustc_middle` is rustc’s shared middle-layer definitions crate: `lib.rs` establishes the crate and exposes the compiler subsystems that carry semantic information from HIR through type checking, trait solving, MIR, and into later analysis, diagnostics, metadata, and code generation. At its foundation, `arena.rs` defines the arena-allocation contract for long-lived middle-layer data, while `macros.rs` supplies crate-wide ICE and boilerplate traversal/lifting macros, `error.rs` provides reusable structured diagnostics for middle-layer analyses, `lint.rs` defines the shared lint-level and lint-emission model, `metadata.rs` encodes cross-crate module/reexport summaries, `values.rs` defines query fallback values and cycle-reporting behavior, and `tests.rs` supplies crate-level test-linkage scaffolding.

Within that crate framework, `ty` is the central type-system layer: it owns `TyCtxt`, interned type representations, generic arguments, items, layouts, folding/visiting/relating operations, persistence support, and diagnostics/provider wiring that the rest of the compiler builds on. `query` declares the full query interface and key space that names, keys, caches, and incrementally tracks compiler computations, while `dep_graph` supplies the middle-layer dependency-node model and stable fingerprinting that connect those queries to incremental compilation and dependency tracking. `infer` contributes the query-stable representation of inference variables, canonical forms, and member/region/const constraints used to move inference state across solver and query boundaries. `traits` defines the shared trait-system model, query payloads, classic selection data, specialization graph, Chalk bridge, elaboration utilities, and structural impls used for trait resolution and type operations.

For IR and semantic program structure, `hir` exposes the local-crate HIR map, traversal filters, shared HIR data/provider wiring, and HIR-level place reasoning for middle-layer consumers. `thir.rs` defines the THIR data model itself—the typed high-level IR between HIR and MIR—and the `thir` module contributes the canonical visitor/walk infrastructure for traversing that IR. `mir` defines the typed Mid-level IR, its bodies, control-flow structure, visitors, semantic helpers, patching, query result types, monomorphization metadata, debug/Graphviz/span views, coverage metadata, and interpreter/const-eval memory model and errors. `middle` gathers additional shared compiler analyses and metadata between front-end checking and later stages, including codegen-relevant attributes, linkage/export and visibility data, region-scope and lifetime structures, language-item/stability accessors, compiler limits, library-feature tracking, and provider registration. `util` rounds out the crate with common formatting and bug-reporting helpers.

Together, these root files and modules make `rustc_middle` the compiler’s canonical semantic data layer: it defines the core IRs, types, queries, dependency tracking, inference and trait-solving interfaces, diagnostics, lint and metadata support, and shared utilities that allow the rest of rustc to analyze programs consistently, incrementally, and across crate boundaries.
